_meta.purpose: Pre-resolved registry values for downstream agents. Agents consuming this file do NOT need to load raw registry files.

spec_identity.notes: New spec family for exterior engineered wood siding (LP SmartSide, T1-11, OSB-based) prime+paint. Context prefix ENSD (ENgineered SiDing) — no collision with existing prefixes. SDNG_ is taken by SF_WOOD_SIDING_EXT_NC_PAINT, FCSD_ is taken by SF_SIDING_FIBERCEMENT_EXT_NC. Combined prime+finish in single spec (same mobilization). KEY DIFFERENCES from fiber cement (FCSD): no alkali-resistant primer, spray_backroll is valid/mandatory for T1-11 and textured profiles, uses SS_EXT_BARE_WOOD not SS_EXT_BARE_FIBERCEMENT, standard acrylic primer only.

paintable_items.name: Exterior siding field surface
paintable_items.notes: REUSED from SF_WOOD_SIDING_EXT_NC_PAINT and SF_SIDING_FIBERCEMENT_EXT_NC. Same physical item (siding field), different substrate material (engineered wood vs natural wood vs fiber cement). Profile modifier (lap/panel/t1_11) adjusts effective surface area and production rate. Update used_in array to include SF_SIDING_ENGINEERED_EXT_NC.

task_prefix.collision_check: No collision. Existing prefixes: CLOSET_SHELF, FRAME, DOOR, CEIL, WALL, TRIM, WIN, STRS, WNSC, WDWL, WDCL, ARCH, BLTN, CABT, SDNG, FCSD. ENSD is unique.
task_prefix.naming_rule: TSK_ENSD_{ACTION} — action should be verb-based. Examples: TSK_ENSD_WASH_LOW_PRESSURE, TSK_ENSD_SEAL_CUT_EDGES, TSK_ENSD_PRIME_SPRAY, TSK_ENSD_FINISH_SPRAY_1, TSK_ENSD_FINISH_SPRAY_BACKROLL_1, TSK_ENSD_SAND_INTERCOAT

expected_modules.notes: Protection setup — landscape, hardscape, HVAC, light fixtures
Low-pressure wash, edge seal cut ends, caulk siding-to-trim joints (NOT butt joints), light sand, moisture check

Field prime — 3 paths: standard acrylic (factory-primed/bare wood), bonding (factory-finished ExpertFinish). NO alkali-resistant primer path (engineered wood is NOT alkaline). spray_backroll valid for textured profiles.
First finish coat — spray or spray_backroll (mandatory for T1-11/textured) or brush_roll (fallback)
Intercoat inspection, light sand (QT4 only), dust removal
Second finish coat — same method as first coat

paintscope_keys.description: Net paintable siding field area (square feet)
Boolean flag confirming new construction context. Always true for this NC spec. Used for engine validation — prevents accidental assignment to repaint projects.
paintscope_keys.notes: Already registered by SF_SIDING_FIBERCEMENT_EXT_NC resolution. This spec reuses it.

paintscope_keys.description: Linear feet of house perimeter where landscape is adjacent and requires protection. Measured along the foundation/siding line, not landscape area.
Count of exterior light fixtures to mask
Count of HVAC condenser units to cover

required_when.condition: light fixtures mounted on/adjacent to siding

input_declarations.description: Exterior light fixture count for masking

substrate_states.notes: SS_EXT_BARE_FIBERCEMENT is NOT valid for this spec — that is fiber cement only. Engineered wood bare surfaces use SS_EXT_BARE_WOOD. SS_EXT_PRIMED_FACTORY is the dominant NC state. SS_EXT_FACTORY_FINISHED covers ExpertFinish products damaged during construction. All SS_EXT_* states exist in controlled_enums.json (added with fiber cement/wood siding specs).

config_dimensions.notes: QT5 excluded — not applicable to siding field per Exterior_Substrates_Doctrine §5.4. QT5 reserved for fine exterior millwork.

KEY DIFFERENCE from fiber cement: spray_backroll is VALID and MANDATORY for T1-11 and textured profiles. Fiber cement avoids back-rolling. Spray is primary for smooth LP SmartSide. Brush_roll is fallback for <750 SF, occupied adjacent, or high wind.
Three engineered wood profiles. T1-11 is unique to this spec (fiber cement has shingle instead). T1-11 mandates spray_backroll application. Lap is fastest, T1-11 is slowest.
Factory-primed is dominant NC state. SS_EXT_BARE_WOOD for cut edges/damaged areas/T1-11 without factory prime. SS_EXT_FACTORY_FINISHED for ExpertFinish products.

quality_tier.notes: QT5 excluded — not applicable to siding field per Exterior_Substrates_Doctrine §5.4.

application_method.notes: spray_backroll is MANDATORY for T1-11 and recommended for textured profiles (cedarmill, roughsawn). This is the KEY DIFFERENCE from fiber cement (which avoids back-rolling). Spray is primary for smooth LP SmartSide lap. Brush_roll is fallback.

sheen.notes: Standard exterior siding sheens. Satin is most common default.

phase.notes: Combined prime+finish spec. No 'apply' phase — uses 'prime' and 'finish' directly.

unit_of_measure.notes: SF is primary UOM for siding field. EA for protection items and edge seal count. LF for caulk joints and landscape perimeter. FIXED for tool cleaning.

substrate_state.notes: SS_EXT_BARE_FIBERCEMENT is NOT valid for this spec. Engineered wood uses SS_EXT_BARE_WOOD. All states exist in controlled_enums.json.

product_role.notes: Sealer for end-cut sealer product. No clear/stain/specialty needed.

protection_level.notes: No full_mask needed — exterior zones use lighter protection levels than interior spray.

surface_ids.notes: All surface IDs exist in id_registry -> surface_ids -> entries_in_active_use. Identical adjacency pattern to fiber cement and wood siding specs.

zone_ids.notes: LF-based landscape protection — proposed by fiber cement sibling resolution. Reusing the same proposed zone.

SYS_EXT_WOOD_PRIMER_BONDING — bonding primer for existing coatings on wood (concept reusable for ExpertFinish)
SYS_EXT_WOOD_FINISH_STANDARD — same product tier, different substrate context
SYS_EXT_WOOD_FINISH_PREMIUM — same product tier, different substrate context
SYS_EXT_FC_PRIMER_ACRYLIC — fiber cement acrylic primer (similar concept but FC-specific warranty)
SYS_EXT_FC_PRIMER_ALKALI — alkali-resistant primer for bare FC (NOT needed for engineered wood)
SYS_EXT_FC_PRIMER_BONDING — bonding primer for ColorPlus (same concept as ExpertFinish)

proposed_systems.name: Standard Acrylic Field Primer for Engineered Wood Siding
proposed_systems.notes: 100% acrylic exterior primer. NOT alkali-resistant (engineered wood is NOT alkaline). Covers both factory-primed and bare wood states. Field prime is MANDATORY per LP SmartSide warranty.

proposed_systems.name: Bonding Primer for Factory-Finished Engineered Wood (ExpertFinish)
proposed_systems.notes: Required for LP SmartSide ExpertFinish factory-finished products damaged during construction. Cured baked finish is non-standard substrate for field paint adhesion.

proposed_systems.name: Standard Exterior Acrylic Finish for Engineered Wood Siding
proposed_systems.notes: 100% acrylic exterior latex from LP SmartSide-approved product list. Must have minimum 15-year paint manufacturer warranty. QT2 may use single coat on primed surfaces.

proposed_systems.name: Premium Exterior Finish for Engineered Wood Siding
proposed_systems.notes: Premium LP-approved materials with 25+ year warranty. Light sand between coats. Raking light inspection.

material_system_prefix.notes: 2 substrate-driven primers + 2 QT-driven finish systems. No QT5 (excluded for siding field). NO alkali-resistant primer path — this is the KEY DIFFERENCE from fiber cement. Engineered wood is wood-based (neutral pH), not cementitious (pH 13.0). Products must be LP SmartSide-approved (different approved list than James Hardie).

proposed_consumables.name: Engineered Wood End-Cut Edge Sealer (LP SmartSide Cut End Seal)
proposed_consumables.notes: LP SmartSide-specific end-cut sealer. Seals field-cut edges to prevent moisture intrusion into OSB core — prevents irreversible springback. Most critical consumable for this spec.

proposed_consumables.name: Airless Spray Tip 517 (lap/panel/T1-11 siding)
proposed_consumables.notes: 515 or 517 for lap siding, 517 for panel/T1-11. Standard tip selection for exterior latex on siding.

proposed_consumables.name: 18-inch Roller Cover for Back-Rolling
proposed_consumables.notes: Required for spray_backroll application method. 3/8" to 1/2" nap for smooth-to-moderate texture. Used to distribute spray-applied coating into T1-11 grooves and textured profiles.

proposed_consumables.name: Exterior Flexible Paintable Caulk
proposed_consumables.notes: Polyurethane or siliconized acrylic for siding-to-trim joints only. Do NOT caulk field butt joints (moisture trap per RF-012).

proposed_consumables.name: 60-Mesh Spray Filter (Black) for Latex
proposed_consumables.notes: Standard 60-mesh (black) filter for latex exterior coatings through airless equipment.

coating_system_ids.notes: See material_system_prefix.proposed_systems for full system definitions.

proposed_configurations.description: 1 prime + 2 finish coats — standard NC sequence at QT3/QT4
1 prime + 1 finish coat — economy QT2 on unprimed surfaces
2 finish coats only — when field prime already applied (SS_EXT_PRIMED_FIELD)
1 finish coat only — economy QT2 on field-primed surface

proposed_profiles.description: Acrylic primer coverage on engineered wood — 300-350 SF/gal smooth, adjusted by surface_factor for textured (cedarmill/roughsawn). Slightly faster coverage than fiber cement (non-porous face on factory-primed).
Primer coverage on bare engineered wood — 250-300 SF/gal. Bare OSB-core face is more porous than factory-primed surface.
Finish coat coverage on primed engineered wood — 300-400 SF/gal smooth, adjusted by surface_factor for textured.

proposed_modifiers.description: Production rate modifier by siding profile
proposed_modifiers.notes: Lap is baseline. Panel slightly slower (large flat areas, fewer joints). T1-11 is dramatically slower (mandatory back-rolling into grooves, constant repositioning). T1-11 factor higher than fiber cement shingle (2.00) because T1-11 has vertical groove geometry requiring roller work at every groove.

proposed_modifiers.description: Material and production modifier by surface texture
proposed_modifiers.notes: Applies to BOTH material quantity and production rate. Textured profiles absorb more product and spray slower. Same factors as fiber cement — texture geometry determines consumption, not substrate material.

adjacent_surfaces.notes: Soffit underside at eave. Often different color. Separate scope.
Frieze board at siding-soffit junction. Separate trim scope.
Corner boards frame siding field. Separate trim scope.
Window casing trim around openings. Separate spec.
Foundation below siding. Not painted in siding scope.

site_condition_rules.notes: Applied per elevation. A project may have different access types on different elevations.

excludes: Window and door protection during siding work — owned by window/door specs
Exterior trim (corner boards, frieze, window/door casing) — separate trim spec
Environmental conditions estimation — excluded from modifiers per RC-003 (SOP reference only)

cross_spec_coordination.notes: No cross-spec flags needed. Window/door protection NOT this spec's responsibility (RC-001 from wood siding). Trim, soffit, and fascia are separate scopes.

proposed_modifiers.description: Production rate modifier by siding profile
proposed_modifiers.notes: Lap baseline. Panel slightly slower. T1-11 dramatically slower due to mandatory back-rolling into vertical grooves.

proposed_modifiers.description: Material and production modifier by surface texture
proposed_modifiers.notes: Applies to BOTH material quantity and production rate.

cross_file_threading: RULE 1: Every TSK_ in sop_modules.json MUST have a matching rate in production.json
RULE 2: Every ITM_ in spec.json MUST appear in at least one variant
RULE 3: Every SYS_ quality_tier MUST match spec.json configuration_dimensions
RULE 4: Every IN_ input in spec.json SHOULD be consumed by sop_modules or production
RULE 5: Every PS_ key in production.json MUST match spec.json required_paintscope_inputs
RULE 6: Every zone_id in spec.json MUST match sop_modules.json protection_metadata.zones
RULE 7: Module phase order: setup -> prep -> prime -> apply -> interstage -> finish -> cleanup
RULE 8: UOM for a task MUST match between sop_modules.json and production.json
RULE 9: All TSK_ IDs MUST use TSK_ENSD_ prefix (from this resolution)
RULE 10: ITM_SIDING_FIELD MUST be used exactly as registered (existing ID)
RULE 11: Downstream agents MUST use only enum values from this resolution's applicable_enums
validation_notes: CRITICAL: Engineered wood is NOT alkaline — do NOT use alkali-resistant primer. Standard 100% acrylic exterior primer is correct for all non-factory-finished substrate states.
CRITICAL: spray_backroll is MANDATORY for T1-11 profile and recommended for cedarmill/roughsawn textures. This is the OPPOSITE of fiber cement (which avoids back-rolling).
CRITICAL: SS_EXT_BARE_FIBERCEMENT must NEVER appear in this spec — that is a fiber cement-specific state. Use SS_EXT_BARE_WOOD for bare engineered wood.
IMPORTANT: T1-11 profile is unique to this spec — fiber cement has HardieShingle instead. T1-11 has vertical groove geometry requiring roller distribution of coating.
IMPORTANT: LP SmartSide-approved product list is DIFFERENT from James Hardie-approved list. Materials Manager must verify LP-specific product approvals.
IMPORTANT: Edge seal is the MOST CRITICAL prep task — unsealed cut edges lead to irreversible OSB core springback (FM-001).
NOTE: Surface texture (smooth/cedarmill/roughsawn) is a MODIFIER, not a configuration dimension — it does not change task structure or module sequence.
NOTE: No power washing on engineered wood — low-pressure water spray only (garden hose + soft brush).

registry_additions_proposed.name: Exterior Engineered Wood Siding Prime and Paint
registry_additions_proposed.justification: New spec family for engineered wood siding (LP SmartSide, T1-11, OSB-based). Distinct from SF_WOOD_SIDING_EXT_NC_PAINT (natural wood substrate) and SF_SIDING_FIBERCEMENT_EXT_NC (cementitious substrate). Different primer requirements (no alkali-resistant), different application method constraints (spray_backroll valid), different siding profiles (t1_11 instead of shingle), different failure modes (OSB core springback vs capillary wicking).

registry_additions_proposed.name: Engineered wood siding task prefix
registry_additions_proposed.justification: New context prefix for engineered wood siding tasks. No collision with existing prefixes (SDNG, FCSD, etc.).

registry_additions_proposed.name: Standard Acrylic Field Primer for Engineered Wood Siding
registry_additions_proposed.justification: Distinct from SYS_EXT_WOOD_PRIMER_ACRYLIC (natural wood) and SYS_EXT_FC_PRIMER_ACRYLIC (fiber cement). Engineered wood has LP-specific warranty requirements and different coverage rates on factory-primed OSB surface.

registry_additions_proposed.name: Bonding Primer for Factory-Finished Engineered Wood (ExpertFinish)
registry_additions_proposed.justification: Analogous to SYS_EXT_FC_PRIMER_BONDING but for LP SmartSide ExpertFinish products. Different factory finish chemistry and substrate.

registry_additions_proposed.name: Standard Exterior Acrylic Finish for Engineered Wood Siding
registry_additions_proposed.justification: LP SmartSide-approved product list is different from Hardie-approved list. Coverage rates on engineered wood may differ from fiber cement and natural wood.

registry_additions_proposed.name: Premium Exterior Finish for Engineered Wood Siding
registry_additions_proposed.justification: QT4 premium system using LP SmartSide-approved premium products.

registry_additions_proposed.name: Engineered Wood Siding Primer Coverage Profile
registry_additions_proposed.justification: Coverage rates on factory-primed engineered wood (300-350 SF/gal) differ from fiber cement (COV_FCSD_PRIMER) due to different surface porosity.

registry_additions_proposed.name: Primer Coverage on Bare Engineered Wood
registry_additions_proposed.justification: Bare OSB-core face is more porous than factory-primed surface — lower coverage (250-300 SF/gal). Distinct from COV_FCSD_PRIMER_ALKALI (which uses alkali-resistant product on bare FC).

registry_additions_proposed.name: Engineered Wood Siding Finish Coat Coverage Profile
registry_additions_proposed.justification: Finish coverage on primed engineered wood (300-400 SF/gal). LP-approved products may have different coverage than Hardie-approved products.

registry_additions_proposed.name: Engineered Wood Siding Profile Production Modifier
registry_additions_proposed.justification: Profile-specific rate modifier: lap=1.00, panel=1.10, t1_11=1.80. T1-11 is unique to this spec and has dramatically different production characteristics than fiber cement profiles.

registry_additions_proposed.name: Engineered Wood Surface Texture Modifier
registry_additions_proposed.justification: Texture modifier: smooth=1.00, cedarmill=1.20, roughsawn=1.30. Same concept as FAC_FCSD_SURFACE_TEXTURE but with ENSD prefix for traceability.

registry_additions_proposed.name: Engineered Wood 1 Prime + 2 Finish Coats
registry_additions_proposed.justification: Standard NC coat sequence for QT3/QT4. Context-prefixed per naming pattern.

registry_additions_proposed.name: Engineered Wood 1 Prime + 1 Finish Coat (Economy)
registry_additions_proposed.justification: QT2 economy coat sequence.

registry_additions_proposed.name: Engineered Wood 2 Finish Coats (Field-Primed)
registry_additions_proposed.justification: For SS_EXT_PRIMED_FIELD at QT3/QT4 — prime already applied.

registry_additions_proposed.name: Engineered Wood 1 Finish Coat (Economy, Field-Primed)
registry_additions_proposed.justification: QT2 on field-primed surface.

registry_additions_proposed.name: Engineered Wood End-Cut Edge Sealer
registry_additions_proposed.justification: LP SmartSide-specific end-cut sealer. Different product from fiber cement edge sealer (CON_FCSD_END_SEALER). Engineered wood sealer must be compatible with OSB core and zinc borate treatment.

registry_additions_proposed.name: Airless Spray Tip 517 for Engineered Wood Siding
registry_additions_proposed.justification: Separate from fiber cement tips — wear profile may differ on wood-fiber substrate vs cementitious. Context-prefixed for traceability.

registry_additions_proposed.name: 18-inch Roller Cover for Back-Rolling Engineered Wood
registry_additions_proposed.justification: Required for spray_backroll method — not needed for fiber cement (no back-rolling). Unique to engineered wood siding workflow.

registry_additions_proposed.name: Exterior Flexible Paintable Caulk for Engineered Wood
registry_additions_proposed.justification: Context-prefixed caulk. Note: siding-to-trim joints ONLY, never field butt joints.

registry_additions_proposed.name: Plastic Sheeting for Exterior Protection
registry_additions_proposed.justification: Context-prefixed protection material.

registry_additions_proposed.name: 60-Mesh Spray Filter for Latex
registry_additions_proposed.justification: Context-prefixed spray filter.
